label: exploratory analytical comparator

scope.task: one binary state, stable world, conditionally independent cues
scope.prior: q0 is calibrated initial knowledge for this benchmark only
scope.bayes: posterior decision maximizing expected correctness after n cues
scope.bounded: initial score +4; each signed cue moves one unit; saturated boundary self-loops; score-zero ties randomize

checks.name: all Markov distributions normalize and remain nonnegative
Bayes expected accuracy is nondecreasing in n
Bayes expected accuracy never falls below the prior
Markov transitions match independent path enumeration at n=10
bounded unit-step updating has at least one prior-erosion case

summary.claim_limit: Freezing can beat misweighted finite-memory updating, but cannot beat optimal cost-free calibrated Bayes in expected accuracy under these benchmark assumptions.

limitations: Conditional cue independence and a stable binary world are benchmark assumptions, not claims about all environments.
The comparator diagnoses the bounded update rule; it does not establish that people or organisms implement Bayes.
The V5 demographic simulations contain feedbacks absent from this one-task accuracy calculation.
